title: Control Plane Routing Playbook — schema, validation, rollout
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the control-plane routing rule configuration: canonical schema, validation rules, and stepwise rollout mechanics across multi-region Redwood deployments. The goal is to have a compact, machine-parseable spec that operators and automation can use to validate, stage, and safely release routing changes (traffic policies, model variant routing, region affinity, fallback chains).

Scope and audience:
- Platform engineers implementing the control-plane APIs
- Release engineers and SREs responsible for rollouts
- Solutions engineers who write customer routing policies

Design goals / constraints (short):
- Human readable + machine enforceable (JSON Schema + light YAML surface)
- Idempotent updates: apply twice == no-op
- Backward compatible: new fields optional with defaults
- Strong validation to avoid accidental cross-region storms or capacity overloads
- Rollout-friendly: support canaries, weighted ramps, automatic rollback triggers

High-level routing concepts used below:
- target: model variant (model_id + version + optional quantization tag)
- region: physical/region affinity (e.g., us-west1, eu-central1)
- policy: match conditions (headers, path, prompt metadata) -> routing decision
- fallback: ordered list of compatible targets if primary fails or is overloaded

Canonical JSON Schema (summary) — used by validation service:
Note: this is an abbreviated schema for readability. The live schema lives in github.com/.../routing-schema.json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id","rules","default"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {"type":"string"},
    "description": {"type":"string"},
    "rules": {
      "type":"array",
      "items": {
        "type":"object",
        "required":["match","action","priority"],
        "properties":{
          "match":{"type":"object"},
          "action":{
            "type":"object",
            "properties":{
              "type":{"enum":["route","split","redirect"]},
              "target":{"type":"string"},
              "weights":{"type":"object"}
            }
          },
          "priority":{"type":"integer"} 
        }
      }
    },
    "default": {
      "type":"object",
      "properties":{
        "target":{"type":"string"},
        "fallbacks":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}
      }
    },
    "metadata": {"type":"object"}
  }
}

YAML config example (what teams will edit):
---
# human-editable routing for web-app-chat feature
id: web-chat-route-v3
description: route chat requests into dedicated pool first, then hosted fallback
rules:
  - priority: 100
    match:
      headers:
        x-customer-tier: enterprise
    action:
      type: route
      target: model:davinci-x-dedicated:2024-09
    region_affinity: [us-west1, us-central1]
  - priority: 80
    match:
      path_prefix: /chat/low-latency
    action:
      type: split
      weights:
        model:davinci-x-dedicated:2024-09: 80
        model:davinci-x-hosted-quant: 20
    region_affinity: [us-west1]
default:
  target: model:davinci-x-hosted-quant
  fallbacks:
    - model:davinci-x-hosted-legacy
    - model:small-chat-embed:stable
---

Validation checklist (automation + human):
- Schema validity: run JSON Schema validator (required). Reject configs with unknown top-level fields unless opt-in header present.
- Referential sanity: every target identifier must exist in model catalog and have a compatible capability tag (e.g., generation vs embeddings).
- Region capacity guardrail: for every region_affinity list, query capacity estimator. If (requested_capacity > available_capacity * 0.6) then reject or require manual approval. Thresholds configurable per customer tier.
- Weight sums: for split actions, weights must sum to 100 (or implicit normalization only if allow-normalize flag set).
- Immutable fields vs updatable fields: id and created_by are immutable. `priority`, `match`, and `action` are updatable but updates that widen traffic (increase counts to a new target) must pass rollout policy.
- Security: configs that reference private-hosted targets must be allowed only from enterprise orgs or approved projects.

Rollout mechanics (recommended automated pipeline):
1) Pre-flight lint: schema + referential checks + capacity guardrail. Fails fast with descriptive errors.
2) Dry-run / simulate: run traffic simulator against historical trace (7d sample) to estimate latency/capacity impact and quality delta. Annotate results in PR.
3) Staging apply: apply config in staging region only. Smoke tests (functional + auth) must pass.
4) Canary apply: deploy to production control-plane but with a traffic match limiting to a small percentage (default 2%). Use route "split" with explicit weights; record snapshot id of config.
5) Monitor window (15–30m): watch SLOs and quality metrics. Minimum required stable window configurable.
6) Automated ramp: if metrics stable, double canary percent each window (2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 16 -> 50 -> 100) until full. Max steps and durations controlled by rollout policy.
7) Rollback: if any failure criteria met (see below) immediately revert to prior snapshot. Rollback must be idempotent and not rely on manual state.
8) Finalize: mark config as active and record audit event + linked PR/owner.

Failure criteria (examples used in automation):
- Error rate delta: +3x or >0.5% absolute increase in 5m error rate for core route
- Latency P50/P95: P95 increases >30% vs baseline and absolute P95 > SLA threshold
- Quality regression: prompt-level quality score drop >3 points (from eval set) or human-review flag > threshold
- Capacity alarm: target region GPU utilization >85% sustained for >2m
- Partial matches: repeated fallback usage >20% of requests for >5m (indicates misroute)

Region migration considerations:
- Explicit region_affinity field: prefer but do not force. If control-plane cannot meet region affinity, action must specify allowed_fallback_regions and a maximum added latency budget.
- Data locality: some customers require strict region-only routing (policy flag: region_strict: true) — these configs require manual approval and additional audit logging.
- Warmup for cold models: when routing will send first traffic to a target with cold cache, orchestrate a pre-warm stage (synthetic warmup requests) prior to canary traffic.

Idempotency and versioning:
- Every config apply produces an immutable snapshot_id (uuid). Snapshot apply must be safe to retry.
- Use optimistic concurrency: writer must present base_snapshot_id; if mismatch, client must rebase and re-run validation.
- Keep full history for 90 days (audit + automated rollback). After 90 days, snapshots can be compacted.

Operational play examples (short):
- Emergency reroute: for region outage, activate a high-priority rule with match: all, action: split -> weights: hosted-100, priority 1000. This rule should be auto-insertable by SRE runbook with a single CLI command.
- Canary to dedicated: create split with 5% to dedicated target; monitor cost + latency; ramp per policy; ensure dedicated autoscaler has headroom before ramp.

Authoring guidelines (for humans editing YAML):
- Keep rules small and focused: prefer multiple rules with priority than a single complex rule.
- Add comments describing intent and known constraints (capacity, expected traffic).
- Link PR to capacity plan and pre-flight simulation output.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should the control-plane support conditional rate limits inside a routing rule (e.g., rate-limit per target)? (TODO: mock API + impact analysis)
- Do we allow cross-model fallback where output types differ (generation -> reranking)? If so, require transform adapters.
- Finalize the exact rollback thresholds used for gold customers vs self-serve customers.

References and pointers:
- schema repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-schema (draft)
- rollout automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-runner
- related doc: CONFLUENCE-1234 (routing design notes)

Quick checklist to ship a routing change (copyable):
- [ ] Update YAML, add description and owner
- [ ] Run pre-flight validator locally
- [ ] Attach simulation output to PR
- [ ] Staging apply + smoke tests green
- [ ] Open canary with snapshot id in PR body
- [ ] Monitor windows green per policy -> ramp -> finalize
- [ ] Tag release in changelog + link to snapshot id

Notes to self: keep this doc short and add examples for inference-only routing (embeddings, reranking) later. Also add a small python helper to compute weight normalization and capacity bucketing.

-- Asha
